I found five functions in `lib/` that call `req.get`. I searched for `.get(` and `.header(` calls, then checked each match to tell request calls from `app.get` and `res.get`.

**`lib/request.js`**: here `this` is the request object, so `this.get(...)` means `req.get`.
- `req.range` (line 213) calls `this.get('Range')`.
- The `protocol` getter (line 318) calls `this.get('X-Forwarded-Proto')`.
- The `hostname` getter (lines 429 and 432) calls `this.get('X-Forwarded-Host')` and `this.get('Host')`.
- The `xhr` getter (line 507) calls `this.get('X-Requested-With')`.

**`lib/response.js`**:
- `res.location` (line 912) calls `this.req.get('Referrer')`.

These don't count:
- The `fresh` getter in `lib/request.js` only calls `res.get`.
- Every other `this.get(...)` in `lib/response.js` is `res.get`.
- `this.get(...)` in `lib/application.js` is `app.get`.
- The `ip`, `ips`, `subdomains` and `protocol` getters also call `this.app.get(...)`, which is `app.get`. That doesn't affect `protocol`, which is listed because of its separate `req.get` call.
- No code in `lib/` calls `req.header`.
